items: The map locates the meter, solar arrays, battery and sprinkler system. The side panel shows site load, solar output and battery charge.
One list shows four electrical measurement points and sprinkler zones A and B. It displays power readings, battery charge and the reported status of each zone.
Zone A has separate start and stop controls for high-pressure washing and rear-panel mist cooling. Both are on standby here, with outputs and simulated feedback off.

title: See the energy.
Understand the change.
Manage the whole site.
intro: A site’s energy story goes beyond its electricity bill. From live monitoring and demand management to storage dispatch, EMS is designed around a complete management cycle, with site data behind each decision.
sceneLabel: Locate equipment on the 3D map and check site load and solar output
story: Equipment starts up and demand rises. At peak time, the team needs to know: what changed, does demand need attention, and could storage help?
When readings, alarms and reports live in different places, each question takes several searches. EMS brings observation, interpretation, management and review into one connected workflow.
steps: Start with the site and its equipment. Review current readings, status and alarms to find changes that need attention.
Compare trends, demand and equipment records. Establish when and under what conditions a change occurred before discussing a strategy.
Bring storage dispatch, event tracking and reporting into one cycle, reviewing how each strategy relates to site operation.
capabilitiesIntro: Find equipment on the 3D map to check readings, review trends or open its controls. The sprinkler demo uses simulated equipment. Supported devices and control conditions depend on the site.
capabilities: Move from a site overview to equipment readings through a shared starting point for daily checks.

Start or stop high-pressure washing and rear-panel mist cooling independently in zones A and B. Compare the control output with simulated feedback for each zone, or stop both zones from the main panel.
Place a change on a timeline and compare operating periods with original records to understand its context.
Consider peaks, demand trends and site objectives together to inform management strategies.
Review storage status, charging needs and site use together to establish workable dispatch conditions.
Follow an event from detection through the underlying records to its handling and review.
Organize operating and management records for a period so different teams can discuss the same evidence.
demoIntro: Choose a step to see the question it addresses and the information to check next.
demoLabel: Interactive workflow illustration · Not live monitoring
demoNote: This example illustrates the energy management workflow. The 3D plant view uses simulated data.
stages: Does today’s energy use look familiar?
Review the overview, then select the equipment and period that need attention.
When did energy use begin to rise?
Compare current readings with historical records to locate the change.
What options do we have at peak time?
Compare demand trends with site objectives before reviewing the operating schedule.
How could storage support the site?
Check storage status, equipment limits and control permissions before discussing a charging strategy.
Connect alarm times, equipment records and handling status to review the sequence.
What should we consider adjusting next?
Bring trends and events together as evidence for the next management review.
